UTxO Pinning: protecting DUST-registered funds in the Dusk wallet

On Midnight, registering a NIGHT coin for DUST generation rotates it into a successor UTxO, and that successor is what generates the DUST that pays every fee. Before this work, an ordinary transfer could silently select and spend that successor, destroying the wallet's fee generation. Pinning makes that impossible by default and deliberate when wanted.

The model

A pin is a protection intent on one UTxO. Every wallet session owns one pin context, keyed by wallet id, network id, and storage namespace, and every spend-capable operation runs through a guarded facade bound to it. Pins carry independent reasons: manual (the user chose to protect the coin) and dust-registration (the wallet protected it automatically because it is the live successor of a confirmed DUST registration).

The rules

  1. Always on. Protection is part of the wallet session; there is no opt-out, no disabled mode, and an unbound facade is refused outright.
  2. Automatic protection follows the chain. When a registration confirms, the wallet identifies the live successor from confirmed chain lineage (never a pre-rotation id) and pins it with reason dust-registration.
  3. Ordinary spending never touches pins. Coin selection excludes every pinned UTxO. When a payment fails only because pinned funds would have covered it, the wallet returns one stable, JSON-safe error, INSUFFICIENT_UNPINNED_FUNDS, carrying the requested, spendable, and pinned amounts. A genuinely broke wallet still gets the SDK's normal insufficient-funds error.
  4. Spending a pin is explicit. Naming targets ({use: [id]}) authorizes exactly those pins plus unpinned fallback, never any other pin. A missing, spent, or foreign target fails with a stable PIN_TARGET_* code. A separate allowPinned: true mode permits all pins for deliberate sweeps.
  5. Reasons are independent. Confirmed deregistration removes only the automatic reason; a manual pin survives it. A coin stays protected while any reason remains.
  6. Fail closed. Corrupt, unknown, or unreadable pin state puts the wallet in read-only recovery. Spending resumes only after a validated restore or an acknowledged reset followed by reconciliation against confirmed chain state. A rejected write never mutates what the wallet believes.
  7. Durable in the browser. Pin state lives in IndexedDB with transaction-committed writes and cross-tab exclusion via Web Locks. Reloading the page brings back the same pins, reasons, and protection.
  8. Failures compensate. A build failure after inputs are booked releases them in reverse order; release outcomes are exact: released, already-released, already-submitted, already-settled.
